Capo Transposer

See what chord your guitar shapes really play at any capo position — with a full transposition table for every common shape.

–
Sounds as

ShapeSounds as

Pure transposition math: shape root + capo semitones = sounding chord. Quality (major/minor/7th) never changes.

📖 How to use

  1. Pick a chord shape you know how to play.
  2. Drag the capo slider to your capo position.
  3. See the resulting chord name instantly.
  4. Check the table for every shape at that capo.

❓ Frequently asked questions

How does capo transposition work?

A capo raises every string by the same number of semitones, so a shape's root note moves up by the capo number. The chord quality (major/minor/7th) stays the same.

Which chord shapes are included?

The 12 most common open shapes: C, A, G, E, D, F, Am, Em, Dm, plus the 7th shapes C7, G7, D7, A7, E7, B7.

Does it need audio?

No — it's pure music-theory math computed in your browser.
